for self-repair, negating the benefits of early signal detection.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"In a large service, strict internal redundancy is usually homogeneous, and all redundant components are coupled to the same internal dependencies. A localized fault in a shared dependency is invisible to monitoring systems because all redundant backups fail simultaneously or are masked by failover. This establishes a 'reliability monoculture'. In a decentralized network, diverse actors generally adopt heterogeneous dependencies, which raises the baseline rate of isolated failures. This increased noise actually strengthens the system against hidden common causes: a shared dependency failure is statistically more likely to strike a minority subset of services, allowing the rest to survive and, crucially, providing an observable, non-correlated signal BEFORE a global catastrophe occurs.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
